sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: For the most part, we take time for granted.
sentences.zh: 在很大程度上，我们把时间视为理所当然。

sentences.en: Maybe we don't have enough of it, but at least we know how it works.
sentences.zh: 也许我们觉得时间不够用，但至少我们知道它是如何运作的。

sentences.en: At least, you know, most of the time.
sentences.zh: 至少，你知道，大多数时候是这样。

sentences.en: A lot of what we think about time and how we keep track of it is relatively recent,
sentences.zh: 我们对时间的许多看法以及我们记录时间的方式都相对较新，

sentences.en: and some aspects that we take for granted aren't actually all that universal.
sentences.zh: 而我们视为理所当然的一些方面实际上并非那么普遍。

sentences.en: And today, we're going to be talking to a few of my 99PI colleagues
sentences.zh: 今天，我将与我的几位《99%隐形》同事交谈，

sentences.en: for a set of mini-stories about our evolving relationship with time.
sentences.zh: 讲述一系列关于我们与时间不断演变的关系的小故事。

sentences.en: And to get us started, it's Kirk Kolstad, the co-author of The 99% Invisible City.
sentences.zh: 首先登场的是《99%隐形城市》的合著者柯克·科尔斯塔德。

sentences.en: And in our book, we wrote about the standardization of time that came with the rise of railroads.
sentences.zh: 在我们的书中，我们写到了随着铁路兴起而出现的时间标准化。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And before standard times,
sentences.zh: 在标准时间出现之前，

sentences.en: rail companies had to juggle all of these city-specific time zones.
sentences.zh: 铁路公司必须处理所有这些城市各自的时区。

sentences.en: But there's one really neat artifact in particular from that period,
sentences.zh: 但那个时期有一个特别精巧的文物，

sentences.en: which really brings the point home.
sentences.zh: 它真正地说明了这一点。

sentences.en: So here's this old ornate clock that hangs on the facade of the Bristol Corn Exchange building
sentences.zh: 在英国布里斯托尔谷物交易所大楼的立面上，

sentences.en: in England.
sentences.zh: 挂着一个古老而华丽的时钟。

sentences.en: So this is a lovely clock with red letters and red hands,
sentences.zh: 这是一个带有红色字母和红色指针的可爱时钟，

sentences.en: except for there seems to be kind of what looks like a long black,
sentences.zh: 只是上面似乎有一个看起来很长的黑色指针，

sentences.en: you know, almost like a second hand potentially.
sentences.zh: 你知道，几乎就像一个潜在的秒针。

sentences.en: But, you know, I can't quite make sense of what it's for.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我不太明白它是用来做什么的。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: One could definitely think that's the second hand,
sentences.zh: 人们肯定会认为那是秒针，

sentences.en: but it's actually a second minute hand.
sentences.zh: 但实际上它是第二个分针。

sentences.en: So there are two different minute hands,
sentences.zh: 所以有两个不同的分针，

sentences.en: and they're set about 10 minutes apart from each other.
sentences.zh: 它们之间相差大约10分钟。

sentences.en: And they're painted those different colors so that, you know,
sentences.zh: 它们被漆成不同的颜色，这样，你知道，

sentences.en: people on the streets below can tell them apart.
sentences.zh: 街上的人们就能把它们区分开来。

sentences.en: So does this second minute hand also have to do with trains?
sentences.zh: 那么这个第二个分针也和火车有关吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So they have this one hand that's for Bristol.
sentences.zh: 所以他们有一个指针是针对布里斯托尔的。

sentences.en: And then when train travel started becoming more commonplace,
sentences.zh: 然后当火车旅行变得越来越普遍时，

sentences.en: they added a second minute hand to show London time.
sentences.zh: 他们增加了一个第二个分针来显示伦敦时间。

sentences.en: And that's the one that's colored black.
sentences.zh: 那就是那个黑色的指针。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So one hand is for locals.
sentences.zh: 所以一个指针是给当地人看的。

sentences.en: They're still on the local time.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然使用当地时间。

sentences.en: The other is for people traveling in and out of the city.
sentences.zh: 另一个是给进出城市的人准备的。

sentences.en: And presumably that the local time is based on high noon
sentences.zh: 据推测，当地时间是基于正午的，

sentences.en: when the sun is highest in the sky.
sentences.zh: 也就是太阳在天空中位置最高的时候。

sentences.en: That's what we talk about in the book.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在书中所谈论的内容。

sentences.en: How did they get this London time
sentences.zh: 他们是如何得到这个伦敦时间的，

sentences.en: that's shown here in this picture about 10 minutes off?
sentences.zh: 也就是图片中显示的那个相差约10分钟的时间？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So that's the crazy part.
sentences.zh: 这才是最疯狂的部分。

sentences.en: Apparently, they actually sent people out from London
sentences.zh: 显然，他们实际上派人从伦敦出发，

sentences.en: on trains with these precisely tuned watches.
sentences.zh: 带着这些精确校准的手表乘坐火车。

sentences.en: And so that way they could keep clocks like this one up to date on London time.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就能让像这样的时钟保持与伦敦时间同步。

sentences.en: So the railroad used the train network to keep track of time.
sentences.zh: 所以铁路利用火车网络来追踪时间。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's sort of this weird meta phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 这是一种奇怪的元现象。

sentences.en: And so you have these dedicated timekeepers who would arrive in a given town
sentences.zh: 所以你有这些专门的计时员，他们会到达某个城镇，

sentences.en: and then they'd hop off the train and they'd go show their watch to the station master
sentences.zh: 然后跳下火车，把他们的手表给站长看，

sentences.en: because the local railroad operators needed to know the precise time in London.
sentences.zh: 因为当地的铁路运营商需要知道伦敦的精确时间。

sentences.en: And then those same watch-wearing travelers would hop onto another train to a different city
sentences.zh: 然后那些戴着手表的旅行者会跳上另一列火车前往不同的城市，

sentences.en: and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 以此类推。

sentences.en: And they'd go about basically updating clocks all across the country one station at a time.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上就是这样一个车站接一个车站地更新全国各地的时钟。

sentences.en: That is wild.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Imagine all these people riding around just to set clocks.
sentences.zh: 想象一下所有这些人到处跑只是为了设置时钟。

sentences.en: Like everyone's like a cog in their own clock.
sentences.zh: 就像每个人都是自己时钟里的一个齿轮。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: They're just parts of a machine.
sentences.zh: 他们只是机器的一部分。

sentences.en: That's hilarious.
sentences.zh: 这太搞笑了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I love it.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个。

sentences.en: I love it so much.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢了。

sentences.en: And it's so hard for us, you know, today to wrap our minds around the way it was.
sentences.zh: 我们今天很难理解当时的情况。

sentences.en: But really, like up until that point, local time was just the time.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，在那之前，当地时间就是时间。

sentences.en: And so that's just how people went about their days.
sentences.zh: 这就是人们度过一天的方式。

sentences.en: And a lot of folks were pretty reluctant to get on board with these newfangled ideas like standard time.
sentences.zh: 很多人非常不愿意接受像标准时间这样新奇的想法。

sentences.en: So really this like three-handed clock is a relic of that brief moment in time between the old and new when there was an acceptance that standard time was kind of required in some ways,
sentences.zh: 所以这个三针时钟确实是新旧交替时期短暂瞬间的遗物，当时人们在某种程度上接受了标准时间的必要性，

sentences.en: but local time was still preferred.
sentences.zh: 但仍然更喜欢当地时间。

sentences.en: And you were just like in this weird interregnum where both of those things were, you know, equally dominant.
sentences.zh: 你正处于这种奇怪的过渡期，两者同样占据主导地位。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly it.
sentences.zh: 是的，正是如此。

sentences.en: And what struck me in writing about this transition is that railroads really effectively collapsed both space and time.
sentences.zh: 在撰写关于这种转变的内容时，让我印象深刻的是，铁路确实有效地压缩了空间和时间。

sentences.en: And what do I mean by that?
sentences.zh: 我这是什么意思呢？

sentences.en: Well, they made longer journeys go faster, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，它们让长途旅行变得更快了，对吧？

sentences.en: But they also compressed the world into these fewer number of time zones so that suddenly you don't have hundreds of time zones for every city.
sentences.zh: 但它们也将世界压缩成了更少的时区，所以突然之间你不再有每个城市都有数百个时区的情况。

sentences.en: You just have, you know, two dozen spanning the globe.
sentences.zh: 你只有，你知道，横跨全球的二十四个时区。

sentences.en: And meanwhile, local time was this really big headache and increasingly a safety hazard for railway operators because if they got it wrong, even by a few minutes,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，当地时间是一个非常大的头痛问题，对于铁路运营商来说，这越来越成为一种安全隐患，因为如果他们弄错了，哪怕只有几分钟，

sentences.en: trains could literally crash into each other.
sentences.zh: 火车也可能真的会相撞。

sentences.en: And of course, eventually there are global agreements around time and, you know, things became standardized.
sentences.zh: 当然，最终关于时间达成了全球协议，你知道，事情变得标准化了。

sentences.en: But I'm really fond of these quirky exceptions and these little remnants of that interstitial period like this clock in Bristol.
sentences.zh: 但我真的很喜欢这些古怪的例外和那个中间时期的小残余，比如布里斯托尔的这个时钟。

sentences.en: So what follows is a bunch of stories about the struggle of us all being on the same time together, who gets left behind,
sentences.zh: 接下来是一系列关于我们所有人共同处于同一时间所面临的挣扎的故事，谁被抛在了后面，

sentences.en: what individuality gets squashed when everyone tries to sync up and all be at the same place at the same time.
sentences.zh: 当每个人都试图同步并在同一时间出现在同一个地方时，什么样的个性被压制了。

sentences.en: So for our next time story, we're going to be talking to 99PI producer Joe Rosenberg.
sentences.zh: 所以对于我们的下一个时间故事，我们将采访《99%隐形》的制片人乔·罗森伯格。

sentences.en: Hey, Joe.
sentences.zh: 嘿，乔。

sentences.en: Hey, Roman.
sentences.zh: 嘿，罗曼。

sentences.en: So what do you have for us?
sentences.zh: 你给我们带来了什么？

sentences.en: So for this story, we're basically going to start where Kurt left us off, this kind of moment of transition when it comes to timekeeping in Britain.
sentences.zh: 对于这个故事，我们基本上要从柯特结束的地方开始，也就是英国计时方式转变的那个时刻。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Like the rise of the regimented London time.
sentences.zh: 就像那种受管制的伦敦时间的兴起。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And everyone running around with watches being like, this is the time.
sentences.zh: 每个人都带着手表跑来跑去说，这就是时间。

sentences.en: This is it.
sentences.zh: 就是这个。

sentences.en: Like, I know the time.
sentences.zh: 就像，我知道时间。

sentences.en: You don't get with the program.
sentences.zh: 你没跟上节奏。

sentences.en: This is the time.
sentences.zh: 这就是时间。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Because it turns out that there's this one very specific profession from around that period, the middle of the 19th century, that's a variation on that phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 因为事实证明，那个时期，即19世纪中叶，有一种非常特殊的职业，是那种现象的一个变体。

sentences.en: And out of like all of the whimsical, quirky jobs that have ever existed in human history, it's now my favorite.
sentences.zh: 在人类历史上存在过的所有异想天开、古怪的工作中，它现在是我的最爱。

sentences.en: Okay, what is it?
sentences.zh: 好吧，那是什么？

sentences.en: Well, I want you to imagine that you are a factory worker in, say, like Manchester in the 1860s.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想让你想象一下你是19世纪60年代曼彻斯特的一名工厂工人。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And maybe you've moved to the city from the countryside where you were used to just getting up with the sun.
sentences.zh: 也许你从乡下搬到了城市，在那里你习惯了随着太阳起床。

sentences.en: You worked when it was light.
sentences.zh: 天亮时你就工作。

sentences.en: You didn't when it was dark.
sentences.zh: 天黑时你就不工作。

sentences.en: It's pretty simple.
sentences.zh: 这很简单。

sentences.en: But now you have to get up before it's even light because your shift at the local cotton mill starts at like 2 a.m.
sentences.zh: 但现在你必须在天亮之前起床，因为你在当地棉纺厂的轮班时间是凌晨2点。

sentences.en: sharp.
sentences.zh: 准时。

sentences.en: Hmm, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: So the question is, how do you do this?
sentences.zh: 所以问题是，你怎么做到这一点？

sentences.en: How do you wake up?
sentences.zh: 你怎么醒来？

sentences.en: I'm assuming there's no alarm clocks at this point.
sentences.zh: 我假设当时没有闹钟。

sentences.en: There's probably not even widespread watches for this class of people necessarily.
sentences.zh: 对于这类人来说，可能甚至没有普及的手表。

sentences.en: Yeah, no alarm clocks and the watches we'll get to.
sentences.zh: 是的，没有闹钟，至于手表我们稍后再说。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Those things, yeah, they're not cheap or widespread at the very leaSt.
sentences.zh: 那些东西，是的，它们至少并不便宜或普及。

sentences.en: So instead, the solution is that you would rely on a kind of human alarm clock by hiring a knocker-upper.
sentences.zh: 所以，解决方案是你通过雇佣一个“敲门人”来依靠一种人类闹钟。

sentences.en: A knocker-upper.
sentences.zh: 敲门人。

sentences.en: It sounds faintly rude, really, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 听起来有点粗鲁，不是吗？

sentences.en: Out of context.
sentences.zh: 脱离上下文的话。

sentences.en: But it wasn't.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: It was a proper job title, a knocker-upper.
sentences.zh: 这是一个正式的职位名称，敲门人。

sentences.en: So this is Ruth Goodman.
sentences.zh: 这是露丝·古德曼。

sentences.en: She is a UK historian and TV presenter and the author of the books How to Be a Victorian and The Domestic Revolution.
sentences.zh: 她是英国历史学家、电视节目主持人，也是《如何成为维多利亚时代人》和《家庭革命》等书的作者。

sentences.en: Her specialty is everyday life in historical periods.
sentences.zh: 她的专长是历史时期的日常生活。

sentences.en: And she says a knocker-upper was someone with a good watch, meaning back then an accurate watch,
sentences.zh: 她说敲门人是一个有好的手表的人，意味着在当时是一块准确的手表，

sentences.en: who would be paid a small fee by various individual residents of a working class area to wake each of them up at a particular time, depending on when their shift started.
sentences.zh: 他们会从工人阶级居住区的各个居民那里收取少量费用，根据他们轮班开始的时间，在特定的时间叫醒他们每个人。

sentences.en: But naturally, you can't have somebody banging on the door at two o'clock in the morning saying, wakey, wakey, wakey, loud enough to wake all the neighbors.
sentences.zh: 但自然地，你不能让某人在凌晨两点砰砰地敲门说，起床了，起床了，声音大到足以吵醒所有的邻居。

sentences.en: And so the way the knocker-upper would do it is they would go around with this really long,
sentences.zh: 所以敲门人的做法是，他们会带着这种非常长的、

sentences.en: fine cane and just reach up to the upper floors of buildings and lightly tap on their customers' window panes until they woke up.
sentences.zh: 细细的藤条，够到建筑物的高层，轻轻敲击客户的窗玻璃，直到他们醒来。

sentences.en: I can see why this is your favorite job in history.
sentences.zh: 我明白为什么这是你历史上最喜欢的工作了。

sentences.en: This is so delightful.
sentences.zh: 这太令人愉快了。

sentences.en: I love it.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢它。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's like Dickensian, but like nice, you know?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就像狄更斯笔下的场景，但很美好，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so they would just slowly go around to one address at perhaps 4.05 a.m., tap on the upper left window, then move on to the next house at 4.10 a.m.,
sentences.zh: 所以他们会慢慢地走到一个地址，也许是凌晨4点05分，敲左上方的窗户，然后移动到下一家，在凌晨4点10分，

sentences.en: tap on the lower right window, and just go down their liSt.
sentences.zh: 敲右下方的窗户，然后顺着名单走下去。

sentences.en: And always aiming, of course, to tap very gently, but not too gently.
sentences.zh: 当然，总是瞄准轻轻地敲，但又不能太轻。

sentences.en: Some knocker-upper swore blind that you needed a particular, you know,
sentences.zh: 有些敲门人发誓说，你需要一个特定的，你知道，

sentences.en: bit of something on the end of the cane to get the right amount of noise that would wake people up in the room, but not wake people up next door.
sentences.zh: 藤条末端加点东西，才能发出恰到好处的噪音，既能叫醒房间里的人，又不会吵醒隔壁的人。

sentences.en: And that way, if they wanted to wake up cool, they'd also have to pay you.
sentences.zh: 这样，如果他们想醒来，他们也必须付钱给你。

sentences.en: There's no point having one paying customer in the street and the whole street getting the benefit.
sentences.zh: 街上只有一个付费客户而整条街都受益是没有意义的。

sentences.en: And so here, let me show you a photo of a knocker-upper plying their trade.
sentences.zh: 所以，让我给你看一张敲门人从事他们工作的照片。

sentences.en: Oh, this is great.
sentences.zh: 哦，这太棒了。

sentences.en: So this is a long row of houses, connected houses, row houses.
sentences.zh: 这是一排长长的房子，连体住宅，排屋。

sentences.en: And a person on the street with a cane that looks like, I don't know, maybe 15 feet long or something like that, like really something.
sentences.zh: 街上有个人拿着根拐杖，看起来，我不知道，可能有15英尺长或者差不多那样，真的很夸张。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: No, it's a solid, somewhere between 15 and 20 feet long, this giant cane, just to reach up to that second floor.
sentences.zh: 不，那是根实打实的、长约15到20英尺的巨型拐杖，就是为了够到二楼。

sentences.en: And you can see he's just going down this kind of classic London row house, tapping on each window.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到他正沿着这种典型的伦敦排屋走，敲着每一扇窗户。

sentences.en: That's so great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: So I see why you need to use the cane for the second floor.
sentences.zh: 所以我明白为什么二楼需要用拐杖了。

sentences.en: What do they do for the first floor?
sentences.zh: 那他们怎么处理一楼呢？

sentences.en: That seems kind of unnecessary.
sentences.zh: 那似乎有点多此一举。

sentences.en: You'd be like in the middle of the street trying to reach with that thing.
sentences.zh: 你得站在马路中间，试图用那玩意儿去够。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So there was a few different knocking up methods.
sentences.zh: 所以当时有几种不同的叫醒方法。

sentences.en: The cane was just one, depending on where your customers were and what the lay of the land was.
sentences.zh: 拐杖只是其中一种，具体取决于你的客户在哪里以及地形如何。

sentences.en: So some people had like a mallet for ground floor doors.
sentences.zh: 有些人用木槌敲一楼的门。

sentences.en: Others in like company towns might be hired by a mining company to very deliberately wake up everyone at the same time.
sentences.zh: 在一些公司城镇，其他人可能会被矿业公司雇佣，专门负责在同一时间叫醒所有人。

sentences.en: And apparently those knocker uppers, since the whole point was to be as loud as possible, used like one of those wooden clackers that you would see at soccer matches.
sentences.zh: 显然，那些叫醒人，因为目的就是尽可能制造噪音，会用那种你在足球比赛中看到的木制棘轮。

sentences.en: Do you know what I'm talking about?
sentences.zh: 你知道我在说什么吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, I do, actually.
sentences.zh: 知道，我确实知道。

sentences.en: But most knocker uppers, like Ruth said, found ways to be a little more precise.
sentences.zh: 但正如露丝所说，大多数叫醒人找到了更精确的方法。

sentences.en: One very famous knocker upper, she used a pea shooter and she had a little, that hollow tube and she would blow dried peas at the window.
sentences.zh: 有一位非常著名的叫醒人，她用的是吹箭筒，她有一个小小的空心管，会把干豌豆吹向窗户。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Do we know who that person is?
sentences.zh: 我们知道那个人是谁吗？

sentences.en: We actually do.
sentences.zh: 我们确实知道。

sentences.en: That apparently was Mary Ann Smith of East London.
sentences.zh: 那显然是伦敦东区的玛丽·安·史密斯。

sentences.en: And there's also a really charming photo of her.
sentences.zh: 而且还有一张关于她非常迷人的照片。

sentences.en: Let me show you that one, too.
sentences.zh: 我也给你看看那张。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: This is so great.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: So she's just there with her pea shooter, her hands in her cardigan, which I'm assuming holds the pebbles or peas that she is shooting.
sentences.zh: 她就站在那儿，拿着吹箭筒，手插在开衫里，我猜里面装着她要发射的鹅卵石或豌豆。

sentences.en: Yeah, her cheeks are like puffed out.
sentences.zh: 是啊，她的脸颊鼓鼓的。

sentences.en: Exactly, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错，是啊。

sentences.en: Like she's in mid pea shoot.
sentences.zh: 就像她正吹到一半一样。

sentences.en: That's so good.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: Oh, it's so good.
sentences.zh: 哦，太棒了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: It's really fascinating the way official regiment of time is just kind of proliferating.
sentences.zh: 官方的时间管理方式正在不断扩散，这真的很迷人。

sentences.en: And it hasn't quite reached into the bedroom of the working class, but it's reached just as far as their window.
sentences.zh: 它还没有完全进入工人阶级的卧室，但已经触及了他们的窗户。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And in addition to it kind of spreading practically, it was also spreading culturally in the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 除了在实践中传播，它在19世纪也在文化上蔓延开来。

sentences.en: People were getting really into being very precise about what time it was.
sentences.zh: 人们开始非常热衷于精确掌握时间。

sentences.en: Ruth says it was just seen as the modern forward thinking thing to do.
sentences.zh: 露丝说，这被视为一种现代的、前瞻性的做法。

sentences.en: And she says one fun example in her own research where she could kind of see this playing out is actually the Jack the Ripper case.
sentences.zh: 她说在她自己的研究中，一个有趣的例子就是“开膛手杰克”案，她能看出这种趋势的影响。

sentences.en: And going through all those police reports was extraordinary because there they are at the end of the 19th century saying at 9.16.
sentences.zh: 翻阅那些警察报告真是非同寻常，因为在19世纪末，他们竟然精确到9点16分。

sentences.en: And I'm thinking 9.16, that's ridiculously accurate.
sentences.zh: 我在想，9点16分，这精确得离谱。

sentences.en: You know, and then they're saying like six minutes later this happened and 14 minutes later that happened.
sentences.zh: 你知道，然后他们说六分钟后发生了什么，14分钟后又发生了什么。

sentences.en: There is no way a watch from that era could possibly be giving you quite that accuracy.
sentences.zh: 那个时代的怀表根本不可能提供这种精确度。

sentences.en: And the people who were making these statements weren't even carrying watches.
sentences.zh: 而且那些做陈述的人甚至都没带表。

sentences.en: So the reports of Jack the Ripper, they're just making it up?
sentences.zh: 所以关于开膛手杰克的报告，他们只是在编造？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Like he just heard the church bells ring maybe a quarter of an hour ago and he's just like winging it.
sentences.zh: 就像他可能在15分钟前听到了教堂钟声，然后就在那儿瞎猜。

sentences.en: But he doesn't choose a nice round number.
sentences.zh: 但他没有选择一个漂亮的整数。

sentences.en: He chooses a very precise number because it lends authority to his statement.
sentences.zh: 他选择了一个非常精确的数字，因为这能让他的陈述显得更有权威性。

sentences.en: So the idea that you could be that precise was culturally enticing, but not actually practically possible.
sentences.zh: 所以，能够如此精确的想法在文化上很诱人，但在实践中并不可能实现。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: If you want to give legitimacy to your testimony, make it really precise.
sentences.zh: 如果你想让你的证词具有合法性，就把它说得非常精确。

sentences.en: It totally makes sense, but it's really funny.
sentences.zh: 这完全说得通，但真的很有趣。

sentences.en: You know, yeah, it really is.
sentences.zh: 你知道，是啊，确实如此。

sentences.en: And so, of course, in this kind of cultural environment where you would rather lie than be caught not knowing the exact time, pocket watches are like really coveted iteMs.
sentences.zh: 所以，在这种文化环境下，你宁愿撒谎也不愿被发现不知道确切时间，怀表成了非常令人垂涎的物品。

sentences.en: It was the, the must-have bling, you know, techno bling.
sentences.zh: 那是必备的炫耀资本，你知道，科技炫耀。

sentences.en: But they were pricey.
sentences.zh: 但它们很贵。

sentences.en: So from about the 1860s, you start to see little businesses setting up with people who have got some sort of timepiece giving time information to other people.
sentences.zh: 所以从1860年代左右开始，你开始看到一些小生意兴起，拥有某种计时器的人会向其他人提供时间信息。

sentences.en: And so this is when the knocker-upper business is really in its heyday, where every urban working class neighborhood had its own knocker-upper.
sentences.zh: 这就是叫醒人行业真正鼎盛的时候，每个城市工人阶级社区都有自己的叫醒人。

sentences.en: And that person would invest in a good, accurate timepiece, almost like someone invested in a taxicab medallion,
sentences.zh: 那个人会投资一个准确的计时器，就像有人投资出租车牌照一样，

sentences.en: and then embark on this career and hope to pay that timepiece off and eventually start turning a profit.
sentences.zh: 然后开始这份职业，希望能还清计时器的钱，并最终开始盈利。

sentences.en: And was it considered a good career?
sentences.zh: 那这被认为是一份好工作吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I know that having a watch was a high-status symbol, but, like, was being a knocker-upper a high-status symbol job?
sentences.zh: 我是说，我知道拥有手表是一种高地位的象征，但叫醒人是一份高地位的工作吗？

sentences.en: Like, could you make money in it?
sentences.zh: 就是说，能靠这个赚钱吗？

sentences.en: Well, I asked Ruth about that, and she told me you might charge each client maybe, like, six pence per week, which, of course, meant nothing to me.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我问过露丝，她告诉我你可能向每个客户收取每周六便士左右的费用，当然，这对我也没什么意义。

sentences.en: Is that a lot, I guess?
sentences.zh: 那是很多吗？

sentences.en: Or is that within, is that reasonable?
sentences.zh: 或者说这在合理范围内吗？

sentences.en: I'm curious if that's like a...
sentences.zh: 我很好奇这是否算……

sentences.en: I mean, yeah, it's sort of reasonable.
sentences.zh: 我是说，是的，还算合理。

sentences.en: I mean, if you had 20 or 30 clients, then you could just about scrape some survival.
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果你有20或30个客户，那你勉强能维持生计。

sentences.en: So it is a profession of desperation, done by people who are really poor, particularly older women, seem to be in a lot of older female knocker-uppers.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种绝望的职业，由非常贫穷的人从事，特别是老年女性，似乎有很多年长的女性叫醒人。

sentences.en: And so it turns out people like Mary Ann Smith of East London were not the exception.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，像伦敦东区的玛丽·安·史密斯这样的人并非个例。

sentences.en: Ruth says that when we think of the Victorian period, we like to think of the women as being strictly in the home.
sentences.zh: 露丝说，当我们想到维多利亚时代时，我们倾向于认为女性严格待在家里。

sentences.en: But the truth is, is that in the lower classes, the number of women earning an income doing heavy manual tasks, hauling bricks, breaking stone, shifting clay, was huge.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，在底层阶级中，有大量女性从事繁重的体力劳动，搬砖、碎石、搬运粘土。

sentences.en: So many of these women will have been physical laborers in their younger years.
sentences.zh: 所以这些女性中有很多在年轻时都是体力劳动者。

sentences.en: And now they've reached a point where they simply can't do that.
sentences.zh: 现在她们到了一个身体实在无法承受的年纪。

sentences.en: The body won't take it anymore.
sentences.zh: 身体已经吃不消了。

sentences.en: And this sort of knocker-upper work is the sort of thing that somebody in that position would take.
sentences.zh: 而这种叫醒人的工作，正是处于那种境地的人会选择的。

sentences.en: And in some ways, this put them in an even more vulnerable position, as you might imagine.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，正如你所想象的那样，这让她们处于更加脆弱的境地。

sentences.en: Walking the streets of London's roughest neighborhoods alone at night.
sentences.zh: 独自走在伦敦最混乱的街区，尤其是在晚上。

sentences.en: So it must have been quite a dangerous job, I would have thought, particularly for an older woman.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这一定是一份相当危险的工作，特别是对一位老妇人来说。

sentences.en: But you'd have to be pretty tough.
sentences.zh: 但你必须足够强硬。

sentences.en: I mean, some of the pictures show some of these people who would take a dog with them, you know, personal security.
sentences.zh: 我是说，有些照片显示这些人中有些会带着狗，你知道，作为个人安保。

sentences.en: And you can't say you blame them.
sentences.zh: 你不能怪他们。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Another interesting group of people who did knocking up, however, are completely different.
sentences.zh: 然而，另一群从事叫醒工作的有趣人群则完全不同。

sentences.en: And that's the police constables.
sentences.zh: 那就是警察。

sentences.en: Oh, so they did like a little side gig for the police constables?
sentences.zh: 哦，所以他们还给警察做点副业？

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: So apparently most police constables did not have a watch, like we mentioned before, at least an accurate watch.
sentences.zh: 显然，大多数警察没有手表，就像我们之前提到的，至少没有准确的手表。

sentences.en: But those that did, if they had a good watch and a night shift, this was something they could do for a little extra cash.
sentences.zh: 但那些有表的人，如果他们有一块好表并且值夜班，这可以作为赚点外快的方式。

sentences.en: They could, yeah, just like moonlight as a knocker-upper.
sentences.zh: 他们可以，是啊，就像兼职做叫醒人一样。

sentences.en: And incredibly, you also see this in the Ripper case.
sentences.zh: 令人难以置信的是，你在开膛手案中也能看到这一点。

sentences.en: The very first victim, Mary Nichols, when the chap found her, he went to find a constable.
sentences.zh: 第一个受害者玛丽·尼科尔斯，当那个人发现她时，他去寻找警察。

sentences.en: He found a constable.
sentences.zh: 他找到了一个警察。

sentences.en: And he told him he'd found this body.
sentences.zh: 他告诉警察他发现了这具尸体。

sentences.en: And the constable was too busy knocking up.
sentences.zh: 但那个警察忙着叫醒客户。

sentences.en: He carried on knocking up.
sentences.zh: 他继续去叫醒别人了。

sentences.en: He didn't come and see the body immediately.
sentences.zh: 他没有立即去查看尸体。

sentences.en: He had clients waiting.
sentences.zh: 他还有客户在等着。

sentences.en: Time is money.
sentences.zh: 时间就是金钱。

sentences.en: You've got to get your knocker-upper job, but the body can wait.
sentences.zh: 你得完成你的叫醒工作，尸体可以等。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, the body can totally wait.
sentences.zh: 哦，是啊，尸体完全可以等。

sentences.en: But, you know, I still like to believe that if only he had not been knocking up, we might know who Jack the Ripper is.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我还是愿意相信，如果他当时没有在叫醒别人，我们可能就知道开膛手杰克是谁了。

sentences.en: The tyranny of time has sort of kept us from knowing Jack the Ripper.
sentences.zh: 时间的暴政在某种程度上阻止了我们了解开膛手杰克。

sentences.en: I mean, it's so interesting.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这太有趣了。

sentences.en: I mean, the way all of these people in these situations are kind of just beholden, you know, culturally and economically to this new form of timekeeping, you know,
sentences.zh: 我是说，所有这些人在这些情况下，在文化和经济上都受制于这种新的计时方式，你知道，

sentences.en: whether they had a way of measuring it or not.
sentences.zh: 无论他们是否有测量时间的方法。

sentences.en: Yeah, and like you said earlier, mechanized time wasn't yet in most people's bedrooms,
sentences.zh: 是啊，就像你刚才说的，机械时间还没有进入大多数人的卧室，

sentences.en: but somehow here it was reaching out and almost literally tapping on their windows because they had to conform to it.
sentences.zh: 但不知何故，它已经触及了他们的窗户，几乎是字面意义上的敲击，因为他们必须顺应它。

sentences.en: Like time was coming for them, whether they liked it or not.
sentences.zh: 就像时间在向他们逼近，不管他们喜不喜欢。

sentences.en: Yeah, and of course, this technology eventually came for the knocker-uppers, too, once we no longer had any use for them.
sentences.zh: 是啊，当然，一旦我们不再需要叫醒人，这项技术最终也会取代他们。

sentences.en: And I actually found an old article from The Guardian from 1914 where they interviewed an unnamed knocker-upper describing the decline of the trade.
sentences.zh: 我实际上找到了一篇1914年《卫报》的旧文章，他们采访了一位未具名的叫醒人，描述了这个行业的衰落。

sentences.en: And he says,
sentences.zh: 他说，

sentences.en: London knocking up isn't what it was.
sentences.zh: 伦敦的叫醒服务已经大不如前了。

sentences.en: At one time, I had 60 clients on my books.
sentences.zh: 曾经，我的账本上有60个客户。

sentences.en: Now I've only 20.
sentences.zh: 现在只有20个了。

sentences.en: And I've bought up the businesses of three others.
sentences.zh: 而且我还收购了其他三个人的生意。

sentences.en: I expect I shall be the last of the knocker-uppers.
sentences.zh: 我估计我将是最后一个叫醒人了。

sentences.en: What can you do when alarm clocks loud enough to summon a fire engine can be bought for half a crown?
sentences.zh: 当闹钟响到足以召唤消防车，而且只要半个克朗就能买到时，你还能做什么呢？

sentences.en: I've knocked up for 30 years and never broken a pane or wrapped on the wrong house, except one.
sentences.zh: 我做了30年的叫醒人，从来没打破过窗户，也没敲错过门，除了那一次。

sentences.en: And they let me get them up for a month before they told me.
sentences.zh: 他们让我叫醒了一个月才告诉我。

sentences.en: And he says that that family never paid up.
sentences.zh: 他说那家人从来没付过钱。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So not only was it a hard job, it got like harder as the years went on.
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅是一份辛苦的工作，而且随着时间的推移变得越来越难。

sentences.en: And he just was so polite, you know, like so polite until the very end.
sentences.zh: 他一直都那么礼貌，你知道，直到最后都那么礼貌。

sentences.en: The whole process seemed incredibly polite with this kind of light tapping on windows.
sentences.zh: 整个过程似乎非常礼貌，就是这种轻轻敲击窗户的方式。

sentences.en: It's sort of sad to see it go by the wayside for blaring alarms in our rooMs.
sentences.zh: 看到它被我们房间里刺耳的闹钟所取代，真是令人难过。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, it almost makes me wish I could be woken up by a knocker-upper myself instead of my iPhone.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我是说，这几乎让我希望自己也能被叫醒人叫醒，而不是被我的iPhone。

sentences.en: But incredibly, some people kind of got this wish because this guy was wrong about one thing.
sentences.zh: 但令人难以置信的是，有些人确实实现了这个愿望，因为这家伙有一件事说错了。

sentences.en: He wasn't the laSt.
sentences.zh: 他不是最后一个。

sentences.en: There are reports that the very, very last of the knocker-uppers in the town of Bolton in northern England didn't retire until 1973.
sentences.zh: 有报道称，英格兰北部博尔顿镇最后一位叫醒人直到1973年才退休。

sentences.en: 1973 was the year before I was born.
sentences.zh: 1973年是我出生前一年。

sentences.en: You are a contemporary, Roman, of knocker-uppers.
sentences.zh: 罗曼，你竟然和叫醒人生活在同一个时代。

sentences.en: That is hilarious.
sentences.zh: 这太搞笑了。

sentences.en: So who was that last knocker-upper?
sentences.zh: 那么最后一位叫醒人是谁呢？

sentences.en: I have not been able to find that out.
sentences.zh: 我还没能查出来。

sentences.en: I don't know their gender or their clients or their method.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他们的性别、客户或方法。

sentences.en: But I'm just really touched that this profession that started out as a kind of harbinger of the forces of change,
sentences.zh: 但我真的很感动，这个最初作为变革力量先驱的职业，

sentences.en: nevertheless turned into a tradition and in the process actually kind of became a time-keeping holdout.
sentences.zh: 最终变成了一种传统，并在过程中实际上成为了一种计时方式的坚守者。

sentences.en: That is lovely.
sentences.zh: 这太美好了。

sentences.en: Well, thank you so much, Joe.
sentences.zh: 好的，非常感谢你，乔。

sentences.en: Thank you, Roman.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，罗曼。

sentences.en: Up next is producer Vivian Leigh.
sentences.zh: 接下来是制片人薇薇安·利。

sentences.en: So ever since COVID started, 99PI went all remote and the staff has kind of scattered across North America.
sentences.zh: 自从新冠疫情开始以来，99PI就完全远程办公了，员工们散布在北美各地。

sentences.en: And so now we have staffers in four time zones, which can be kind of a pain in the ass.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我们在四个时区都有员工，这真是件麻烦事。

sentences.en: But I guess the alternative would be worse.
sentences.zh: 但我猜想，另一种选择可能会更糟。

sentences.en: Like if we were in one time zone, but actually 3,000 miles away.
sentences.zh: 就像我们处于同一个时区，但实际上却相隔 3000 英里。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And that's a story that I have for you right now.
sentences.zh: 而这正是我现在要讲给你们听的故事。

sentences.en: So it's a story about one time zone, a place with only one time zone, and how it's become intertwined with power and politics and freedom.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于时区的故事，一个只有一个时区的地方，以及它是如何与权力和政治以及自由交织在一起的。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, this is dramatic.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这很有戏剧性。

sentences.en: Let's hear it.
sentences.zh: 让我们听听看。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Like, so as you mentioned, very wide countries like the U.S.
sentences.zh: 就像你提到的，像美国这样幅员辽阔的国家，

sentences.en: or Canada or Russia, we have these multiple time zones to break up the day because, you know,
sentences.zh: 或者加拿大或俄罗斯，我们有多个时区来划分一天的时间，因为你知道，

sentences.en: otherwise the amount of daylight in a day would be unevenly distributed depending on how far east or how far west you are.
sentences.zh: 否则一天的日照量会根据你所处的经度位置而分布不均。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But there is a country with a very wide landmass that only uses one official time zone across the entire territory, and that's China.
sentences.zh: 但有一个国土面积非常广阔的国家，整个领土只使用一个官方时区，那就是中国。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: One time zone across the entire country.
sentences.zh: 整个国家只有一个时区。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And according to the Guinness Book of World Records, it's actually the largest country in the world with only one time zone.
sentences.zh: 根据《吉尼斯世界纪录大全》，它实际上是世界上唯一一个只有一个时区的最大国家。

sentences.en: I mean, it's one of the largest countries in the world in general.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它本身就是世界上最大的国家之一。

sentences.en: Yes, I guess so.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想也是。

sentences.en: But how wide is China?
sentences.zh: 但中国有多宽呢？

sentences.en: Like, what are we working with here?
sentences.zh: 我们是在讨论什么规模？

sentences.en: It's roughly as wide as the United States or Canada.
sentences.zh: 它大约和美国或加拿大一样宽。

sentences.en: And as astronomers in China have pointed out many times, it really, by all rights, ought to have five time zones, which generally go every 15 degrees.
sentences.zh: 正如中国的天文学家多次指出的那样，从各方面来看，它本应有五个时区，通常每 15 度一个。

sentences.en: So this is Gardner Bovington.
sentences.zh: 这位是加德纳·博文顿（Gardner Bovington）。

sentences.en: He's an associate professor in the departments of Central Eurasian Studies and International Studies at Indiana University.
sentences.zh: 他是印第安纳大学中欧亚研究系和国际研究系的副教授。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Gardner Bovington?
sentences.zh: 加德纳·博文顿？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Next time I check into a hotel under a pseudonym, I'm going in as Gardner Bovington.
sentences.zh: 下次我用化名登记入住酒店时，我就用加德纳·博文顿这个名字。

sentences.en: That is such a good name.
sentences.zh: 这名字真好听。

sentences.en: That's exactly what I said.
sentences.zh: 我当时也是这么说的。

sentences.en: Has anybody ever told you that you have, like, the perfect name for a podcast guest?
sentences.zh: 有没有人告诉过你，你的名字非常适合做播客嘉宾？

sentences.en: It has been mentioned before.
sentences.zh: 以前有人提到过。

sentences.en: So, awesome.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: So, if Gardner is saying that China should actually encompass five different time zones, why does it operate with only one?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果加德纳说中国实际上应该包含五个不同的时区，为什么它只运行一个呢？

sentences.en: And has it always been like this?
sentences.zh: 而且一直都是这样吗？

sentences.en: No, it hasn't.
sentences.zh: 不，并不是。

sentences.en: And actually, timekeeping across the country was sort of all over the place until the end of World War II.
sentences.zh: 事实上，直到二战结束前，全国的时间记录都相当混乱。

sentences.en: And for a brief period of time, they actually did observe five time zones across the country.
sentences.zh: 在一段短暂的时间里，他们确实在全国范围内实行了五个时区。

sentences.en: But that was all thrown out in 1949 after the establishment of the People's Republic of China.
sentences.zh: 但这一切在 1949 年中华人民共和国成立后都被废除了。

sentences.en: So, the Communist Party had just won this long civil war.
sentences.zh: 当时，共产党刚刚赢得了这场漫长的内战。

sentences.en: And leadership thought that having one national time on every clock across China was this very literal way to unite a fractured country.
sentences.zh: 领导层认为，让全中国的每一个时钟都统一为全国时间，是团结这个分裂国家的一种非常直观的方式。

sentences.en: A state has many challenges in trying to touch people in all the parts of the country, what we call the reach of the state.
sentences.zh: 一个国家在试图触及全国各地的人民时面临许多挑战，这就是我们所说的国家影响力范围。

sentences.en: This was a quick, very efficient way to do it, to say there's one time, and it's the time we're using for the entire country.
sentences.zh: 这是一种快速且非常有效的方法，即宣布只有一个时间，这就是我们整个国家使用的时间。

sentences.en: And that time is called Beijing time.
sentences.zh: 而那个时间被称为北京时间。

sentences.en: Which means that when it's 9 a.m.
sentences.zh: 这意味着当北京时间是上午 9 点时，

sentences.en: in Beijing, it's 9 a.m.
sentences.zh: 北京是上午 9 点，

sentences.en: 2,700 miles away in Kashgar.
sentences.zh: 2700 英里外的喀什也是上午 9 点。

sentences.en: Yeah, so one thing I'm struck by is that if you look at a map, Beijing, that's the nation's capital where the national time is based.
sentences.zh: 是的，让我印象深刻的一点是，如果你看地图，北京是国家的首都，全国时间就是以那里为准的。

sentences.en: It's like all the way up in the sort of northeastern part of China.
sentences.zh: 它位于中国东北部，非常偏远。

sentences.en: And so, like, that leaves everyone to the west, like, really, like, if it was centered, at least you would have something to work with.
sentences.zh: 所以，这让西部所有人都……如果它是居中的，至少你还有点回旋余地。

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: But it's really in one extreme location.
sentences.zh: 但它确实位于一个极端的位置。

sentences.en: So how does people in the far west deal with a clock that doesn't match their solar day, like, really at all?
sentences.zh: 那么远西部的人们是如何应对一个与他们的太阳日完全不匹配的时钟的呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, so Gardner is actually a scholar of Xinjiang, which is an autonomous territory in the northwest of China.
sentences.zh: 是的，加德纳实际上是一位研究新疆的学者，新疆是中国西北的一个自治区。

sentences.en: It's really far west, and it's home to about 12 million Uyghurs who are an ethnic minority native to Xinjiang.
sentences.zh: 它位于极西之地，是约 1200 万维吾尔族人的家园，他们是新疆本土的少数民族。

sentences.en: They speak Uyghur and are Muslim, and they're very different culturally from the Han majority, which make up about 92% of the country.
sentences.zh: 他们讲维吾尔语，信奉伊斯兰教，在文化上与占全国人口约 92% 的汉族多数群体截然不同。

sentences.en: And for decades, the Chinese government has worried about separatism in the region,
sentences.zh: 几十年来，中国政府一直担心该地区的分裂主义，

sentences.en: and it's led to pretty severe state-sponsored suppression of Uyghur life and to an ongoing genocide.
sentences.zh: 这导致了国家支持的对维吾尔族生活的严重压迫，并演变成了一场持续的种族灭绝。

sentences.en: I'll get more into this later.
sentences.zh: 我稍后会详细说明这一点。

sentences.en: Okay, okay.
sentences.zh: 好的，好的。

sentences.en: We'll put it in there.
sentences.zh: 我们先记下这一点。

sentences.en: But I wanted to kind of rewind back to the 1990s when Gardner first began traveling to Xinjiang.
sentences.zh: 但我还是想回到 20 世纪 90 年代，当时加德纳第一次开始去新疆旅行。

sentences.en: My first trip to Xinjiang was in 1994.
sentences.zh: 我第一次去新疆是在 1994 年。

sentences.en: He was doing field research in the region, and he realized that there were actually two separate time zones that existed in Xinjiang.
sentences.zh: 他在该地区进行实地考察，意识到新疆实际上存在两个独立的时区。

sentences.en: There was Beijing time, which was the official national time, and this was used by the Han Chinese in the area.
sentences.zh: 一个是北京时间，这是官方的全国时间，当地的汉族人使用这个时间。

sentences.en: But then there was this totally different time that was used by the Uyghur population called Xinjiang time, or local time.
sentences.zh: 但随后还有一种维吾尔族人口使用的完全不同的时间，称为新疆时间或当地时间。

sentences.en: It was only when I started to understand Uyghur that I heard people using this expression for Xinjiang time in Uyghur.
sentences.zh: 直到我开始了解维吾尔语，我才听到人们用维吾尔语表达这种新疆时间。

sentences.en: And then I started thinking, wait a minute, why are they saying that?
sentences.zh: 然后我开始想，等一下，他们为什么要那样说？

sentences.en: Then I started noticing that the time that they used, the numbers they used for time, were two hours off that of Beijing time.
sentences.zh: 接着我开始注意到，他们使用的时间，他们用来表示时间的数字，比北京时间晚了两个小时。

sentences.en: So Beijing time was and still is the official time zone in Xinjiang.
sentences.zh: 所以北京时间过去是，现在仍然是新疆的官方时区。

sentences.en: So things like train stations and government offices, they all run on Beijing's clock.
sentences.zh: 因此，火车站和政府办公室等场所都按照北京时间运行。

sentences.en: And if you were to ask a Han person what time it was, they would tell you in Beijing time.
sentences.zh: 如果你问一个汉族人现在几点，他们会告诉你北京时间。

sentences.en: But Gardner noticed that if a Uyghur person were asked what time it was, they would most likely respond with the, quote, local time, which was two hours behind Beijing.
sentences.zh: 但加德纳注意到，如果问一个维吾尔族人现在几点，他们很可能会回答所谓的“当地时间”，即比北京时间晚两个小时。

sentences.en: And this was because it more closely followed the solar pattern of Xinjiang.
sentences.zh: 这是因为它更贴近新疆的太阳运行规律。

sentences.en: Wow, that is complicated, at least from what Gardner observed back in the 90s.
sentences.zh: 哇，这很复杂，至少从加德纳 90 年代的观察来看是这样。

sentences.en: How did that work in everyday life?
sentences.zh: 这在日常生活中是如何运作的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So take, for example, what we call noon.
sentences.zh: 以我们所说的中午为例。

sentences.en: So like basically when the sun is at its highest point in the day.
sentences.zh: 也就是太阳在一天中位置最高的时候。

sentences.en: If you were to ask someone who was Uyghur what time it was, they might say it was 12 p.m.
sentences.zh: 如果你问一个维吾尔族人现在几点，他们可能会说是中午 12 点。

sentences.en: But if you were to ask someone who was Han, they would probably tell you it was actually 2 p.m.
sentences.zh: 但如果你问一个汉族人，他们可能会告诉你其实是下午 2 点。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So for Han Chinese people in Xinjiang, life is just lived two hours earlier than local time?
sentences.zh: 所以对于新疆的汉族人来说，生活比当地时间早两个小时？

sentences.en: Are they waking up and going to work in the dark and just dealing with the inconvenience?
sentences.zh: 他们是在黑暗中起床去上班，只是为了应付这种不便吗？

sentences.en: And just to keep in step with Beijing, to work Beijing hours?
sentences.zh: 仅仅是为了与北京保持一致，按照北京时间工作？

sentences.en: Yeah, I wondered that too, but no.
sentences.zh: 是的，我也想过这个问题，但并不是。

sentences.en: Since I started out by suggesting Beijing wanted to sort of extend its authority over the whole country and show that it was doing so,
sentences.zh: 既然我一开始就提到北京想要在全国范围内扩大其权威并展示其影响力，

sentences.en: it might make sense for people to get up, right, to be ready at their work unit at 8 or 9 Beijing time and so on.
sentences.zh: 人们起床，在上午 8 点或 9 点北京时间准备好在工作单位上班等等，这似乎是有道理的。

sentences.en: And that might have been so at one time.
sentences.zh: 那可能曾经是这样。

sentences.en: But my impression was in the 1990s and 2000s that that wasn't so, that even Hans, who used Beijing time, shifted two hours.
sentences.zh: 但我的印象是，在 20 世纪 90 年代和 2000 年代，情况并非如此，即使是使用北京时间的汉族人，也推迟了两个小时。

sentences.en: Now, I was curious about this and I asked some people.
sentences.zh: 当时我对这一点很好奇，于是问了一些人。

sentences.en: So the convenience of one time zone is kind of defied by the fact that if a Beijing official calls at 9 o'clock in the morning Beijing time,
sentences.zh: 所以，单一时区的便利性被这样一个事实所打破：如果北京的官员在上午 9 点（北京时间）打电话，

sentences.en: the person in the work unit in Urumqi is not going to be in the office, right?
sentences.zh: 乌鲁木齐工作单位的人根本不会在办公室，对吧？

sentences.en: The person said, well, yeah, but that's understood.
sentences.zh: 那个人说，嗯，是的，但这是心照不宣的。

sentences.en: So Han people actually lived by Xinjiang solar time, even though they used Beijing's clocks to communicate the time.
sentences.zh: 所以汉族人实际上是按照新疆太阳时间生活的，尽管他们使用北京时间的时钟来交流时间。

sentences.en: Like, OK, so, you know, how much did these two time zones bump into each other?
sentences.zh: 就像，好吧，你知道，这两个时区在多大程度上会发生冲突？

sentences.en: Because, I mean, it just sounds so confusing.
sentences.zh: 因为，我的意思是，这听起来太令人困惑了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, kind of.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，某种程度上吧。

sentences.en: So if you're a foreigner and you're meeting up with a local, you should probably specify which time they're using.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是一个外国人，要和当地人见面，你最好明确他们使用的是哪个时间。

sentences.en: I was reading this account from a Han Chinese person who happened to be friends with a lot of Uyghurs.
sentences.zh: 我读过一个汉族人的叙述，他碰巧和很多维吾尔族人是朋友。

sentences.en: And he was annoyed because he would always show up like two hours early for everything.
sentences.zh: 他很恼火，因为他总是比别人早到两个小时。

sentences.en: But Garner said that in most cases,
sentences.zh: 但加德纳说，在大多数情况下，

sentences.en: it wasn't all that confusing because Uyghurs basically knew which clock to refer to by the language that they were speaking or who they were speaking to.
sentences.zh: 这并没有那么令人困惑，因为维吾尔族人基本上知道通过他们所说的语言或交谈的对象来参考哪个时钟。

sentences.en: Like if they were talking to a Uyghur family member or friend, maybe they would say, hey, I'm leaving for work at 8 a.m.
sentences.zh: 比如如果他们是在和维吾尔族的家人或朋友交谈，也许他们会说，嘿，我早上 8 点去上班。

sentences.en: But if they were speaking Mandarin to a Han person, they automatically knew to say, hey, I'm leaving for work at 10 a.m.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们是用普通话和汉族人交谈，他们会自动知道说，嘿，我上午 10 点去上班。

sentences.en: I mean, that sounds just like classic code switching, but that, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这听起来就像典型的语码转换，但是，你知道，

sentences.en: someone who is Uyghur would have to adjust their language depending on the culture of the person they were talking to.
sentences.zh: 一个维吾尔族人必须根据他们交谈对象的文化来调整他们的语言。

sentences.en: And they would know to do it and they would and it would be the onus would be on them to do it.
sentences.zh: 他们会知道这样做，而且责任在于他们去这样做。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: I didn't actually know the word code switching in 1994.
sentences.zh: 我 1994 年其实还不知道“语码转换”这个词。

sentences.en: Today, I think you're spot on.
sentences.zh: 今天，我认为你说得非常准确。

sentences.en: It's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So there are linguistic codes, right?
sentences.zh: 所以有语言代码，对吧？

sentences.en: When a bilingual Spanish English speaker speaks,
sentences.zh: 当一个会说西班牙语和英语的双语者说话时，

sentences.en: she will use the Anglo version of names to convenience English speakers and switch to the Spanish version of names in order not to be mocked by fellow Spanish speakers.
sentences.zh: 她会使用英语名字来方便英语使用者，并切换到西班牙语名字，以免被其他西班牙语使用者嘲笑。

sentences.en: And here we're talking about time codes, switching time codes.
sentences.zh: 而这里我们谈论的是时间代码，切换时间代码。

sentences.en: It is interesting to me that the time of day actually depended on the ethnicity of who you were asking.
sentences.zh: 让我感兴趣的是，一天的时间实际上取决于你询问对象的种族。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: And Gardner says that he thought that this was actually a political statement.
sentences.zh: 加德纳说，他认为这实际上是一种政治声明。

sentences.en: You know, like even in the 1990s for Uyghurs, open dissent could be interpreted as a threat of separatism, which could get you in a lot of trouble with the Chinese government.
sentences.zh: 你知道，即使在 20 世纪 90 年代，对于维吾尔族人来说，公开的异议也可能被解读为分裂主义的威胁，这可能会让你在中国政府那里遇到大麻烦。

sentences.en: But by choosing to set your watch to local time instead of Beijing time, it felt like this quiet and private form of protest or solidarity.
sentences.zh: 但通过选择将手表设置为当地时间而不是北京时间，这感觉像是一种安静而私密的抗议或团结形式。

sentences.en: People might not dare to be openly hostile, openly resistant, openly demonstrate and so forth.
sentences.zh: 人们可能不敢公开敌对、公开反抗、公开示威等等。

sentences.en: And so instead, they'll find little ways, possibly hidden or half hidden, to express their defiance and to show each other that they are defying the government.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会寻找一些小方法，可能是隐藏的或半隐藏的，来表达他们的反抗，并向彼此展示他们正在反抗政府。

sentences.en: And so we could say that keeping one's daily schedule on Xinjiang time and when pressed calling it Xinjiang time and rejecting Beijing time are all modes of everyday resistance.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以说，按照新疆时间安排日常生活，并在被问及时称其为新疆时间并拒绝北京时间，都是日常反抗的模式。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: That is just so fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这真是太迷人了。

sentences.en: But, you know, given the intensity of the news coming out of Xinjiang now, like how safe is it to use Xinjiang time presently?
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，考虑到现在从新疆传出的新闻的强度，目前使用新疆时间有多安全？

sentences.en: Like how secret can you be?
sentences.zh: 你能有多隐秘？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So as you noticed, Gardner's observations of local time versus Beijing time mainly took place in the 1990s and early 2000s.
sentences.zh: 正如你注意到的，加德纳对当地时间与北京时间的观察主要发生在 20 世纪 90 年代和 21 世纪初。

sentences.en: Basically, Gardner is part of a group that calls themselves the Xinjiang 13.
sentences.zh: 基本上，加德纳是一个自称为“新疆 13 人”组织的一员。

sentences.en: They're a group of scholars who have essentially been pretty much barred from entering China because of a scholarly work that they wrote about Xinjiang.
sentences.zh: 他们是一群学者，由于他们撰写的关于新疆的学术著作，基本上被禁止进入中国。

sentences.en: So he hasn't actually been able to return to China since 2005.
sentences.zh: 所以他自 2005 年以来实际上一直没能回到中国。

sentences.en: So that's why most of this comes from like the early 90s or the mid 90s.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么大部分信息来自 90 年代初或 90 年代中期。

sentences.en: But over the past few years, the human rights crisis has escalated severely.
sentences.zh: 但在过去几年里，人权危机严重升级。

sentences.en: It's at the point where the U.S.
sentences.zh: 目前的情况是，美国已经认定，

sentences.en: has determined that what's happening to the Uyghurs in Xinjiang is genocide.
sentences.zh: 在新疆发生的针对维吾尔族的事情是种族灭绝。

sentences.en: Mass internment of up to two million members of the mostly Muslim ethnic minority group, the Uyghurs.
sentences.zh: 大规模拘禁了多达 200 万名主要是穆斯林的少数民族群体成员，即维吾尔族人。

sentences.en: Psychological torture.
sentences.zh: 心理折磨。

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: and other countries have labeled China's treatment of Uyghurs as genocide.
sentences.zh: 和其他国家已将中国对待维吾尔族人的方式定性为种族灭绝。

sentences.en: That China may be expanding its so-called re-education camps.
sentences.zh: 中国可能正在扩大其所谓的“再教育营”。

sentences.en: And among many other human rights violations, a large population of Uyghurs and other Muslim minorities have been detained in what have officially been called, you know,
sentences.zh: 在众多其他人权侵犯行为中，大量维吾尔族和其他穆斯林少数民族被关押在官方称为，你知道的，

sentences.en: vocational education training centers, but are effectively re-education camps.
sentences.zh: 职业教育培训中心的地方，但实际上是再教育营。

sentences.en: I mean, clearly they're camps, which is a distinction between other schools or training centers or prisons as well in some ways.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很明显它们是营地，这在某种程度上区别于其他学校、培训中心或监狱。

sentences.en: But it's very clear from people that have been in them, that have worked in them, they are actually camps, that they're a prison space, a carceral space,
sentences.zh: 但从那些在里面待过、在里面工作过的人那里可以清楚地看出，它们实际上是营地，是监狱空间，是监禁空间。

sentences.en: really a medium security prison.
sentences.zh: 确实是一所中度戒备监狱。

sentences.en: So this is Darren Beiler.
sentences.zh: 这位是达伦·拜勒。

sentences.en: He's an anthropologist at Simon Fraser University, and he studies how ethnic minorities in northwest China are surveilled and policed.
sentences.zh: 他是西蒙菲莎大学的一名人类学家，专门研究中国西北地区的少数民族是如何受到监视和管控的。

sentences.en: He's done a lot of fieldwork in Xinjiang and was last there in 2018.
sentences.zh: 他在新疆做了大量的实地考察，最后一次去是在2018年。

sentences.en: And he says that, you know, because of the pervasiveness of surveillance technology paired with smartphone use, using local time could actually be potentially dangerous.
sentences.zh: 他说，由于监视技术与智能手机的普及，使用当地时间实际上可能存在潜在危险。

sentences.en: I'm sure most people now have their phone set to Beijing time.
sentences.zh: 我相信现在大多数人的手机都设置成了北京时间。

sentences.en: And, you know, most people expect to have their phone checked, to have it scanned, or in some cases they're forced to install nanny apps on their phone,
sentences.zh: 而且，大多数人都预料到自己的手机会被检查、被扫描，在某些情况下，他们甚至被迫在手机上安装监控软件，

sentences.en: which will upload the data that's being collected on their phone.
sentences.zh: 这些软件会上传手机上收集到的数据。

sentences.en: So most people are aware that everything on their phone is basically state property at this point.
sentences.zh: 所以大多数人都意识到，在这一点上，他们手机里的一切基本上都属于国家财产。

sentences.en: And it's not that it's necessarily against the law to use local time, but Darren says that a Uyghur person could be, you know,
sentences.zh: 并不是说使用当地时间一定违法，但达伦说，维吾尔族人可能会，你知道，

sentences.en: putting themselves in a vulnerable position if they had their phone set to anything other than Beijing time.
sentences.zh: 如果他们的手机设置的不是北京时间，就会让自己处于脆弱的境地。

sentences.en: So in the government documents or in documents that are in circulation in the Chinese Internet from Xinjiang, they talk really directly about this issue.
sentences.zh: 在政府文件或中国互联网上流传的新疆相关文件中，他们非常直接地谈到了这个问题。

sentences.en: They say that you should look really carefully at people that are using local time.
sentences.zh: 他们说，应该密切关注那些使用当地时间的人。

sentences.en: They don't say outright that it's illegal necessarily in most cases, but it is certainly something that they're looking at as a sign of suspicion.
sentences.zh: 在大多数情况下，他们并没有直接说这是违法的，但这无疑是他们视为可疑迹象的事情。

sentences.en: And there's a laundry list of things that can be interpreted as a, quote, sign of separatism, like wearing a headscarf, having a beard, having WhatsApp installed on your phone,
sentences.zh: 有一长串的事情可以被解读为所谓的“分裂主义迹象”，比如戴头巾、留胡子、手机上安装了WhatsApp，

sentences.en: or simply speaking to someone who lives abroad.
sentences.zh: 或者仅仅是与居住在国外的人交谈。

sentences.en: These are all things that have gotten people in trouble with the government.
sentences.zh: 这些都是让人们受到政府惩处的事情。

sentences.en: And Darren even said that he noticed people having to self-censor themselves in all these private ways,
sentences.zh: 达伦甚至提到，他注意到人们不得不以各种私下的方式进行自我审查，

sentences.en: like having to change the way that they greet each other over the phone so that they drop Islamic identifiers.
sentences.zh: 比如不得不改变打电话时互相问候的方式，以去掉伊斯兰特征的称呼。

sentences.en: So time is just one example of how these, you know, intimate parts of Uyghur culture are being suppressed.
sentences.zh: 所以，时间只是维吾尔文化中这些私密部分如何被压制的一个例子。

sentences.en: It's a sign of them potentially being separatists, of being, you know, more loyal to their own ethnicity, their own geographic location than the nation.
sentences.zh: 这被视为他们可能具有分裂主义倾向的迹象，即比起国家，他们更忠于自己的民族和地理位置。

sentences.en: And so there's definitely pressure on people to use Beijing time.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们确实面临着使用北京时间的压力。

sentences.en: I mean, when you think about the history of the implementation of one time zone,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当你思考统一时区的实施历史时，

sentences.en: you see it sort of presaging all this other form of suppression that has these differences that are perfectly capable of existing inside of one country.
sentences.zh: 你会发现它预示着所有其他形式的压制，而这些差异完全可以在一个国家内共存。

sentences.en: You know, like time zones can exist inside one country.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像一个国家内完全可以存在不同的时区。

sentences.en: And it's just kind of stunning that they once had five time zones and created one, you know, and what that says about everything else.
sentences.zh: 令人震惊的是，他们曾经拥有五个时区，却硬生生统一成了一个，这说明了一切。

sentences.en: Yeah, and Gardner Bovington from earlier in the piece said that, you know, even from the beginning, it was very clear who wasn't going to fit into a system built on Beijing time.
sentences.zh: 是的，节目早些时候的加德纳·博文顿说，即使从一开始，很明显谁无法适应建立在北京时间基础上的系统。

sentences.en: You design a system of timekeeping that's manifestly at odds with the local experience of the sun's transit through the sky and so reminds people constantly,
sentences.zh: 你设计了一套明显与当地太阳运行轨迹不符的计时系统，这不断提醒人们：

sentences.en: you are at the periphery, you're not in the center.
sentences.zh: 你处于边缘，你不在中心。

sentences.en: Gardner said something kind of interesting, which was like, the reason why it's set to Beijing time is because this is a capital.
sentences.zh: 加德纳说了一件很有趣的事，他说之所以设置为北京时间，是因为那是首都。

sentences.en: This is where the orders emanate.
sentences.zh: 这是命令发出的地方。

sentences.en: This is where you should be looking for leadership.
sentences.zh: 这是你应该寻求领导的地方。

sentences.en: But that really shows how little thought that they put into the people, you know, 3,000 miles away in the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 但这确实表明他们对远在3000英里外西部的人民考虑得有多么少。

sentences.en: Like how little consideration that it took to consider what their days might look like.
sentences.zh: 他们几乎没有考虑过当地人的生活会是什么样子。

sentences.en: And how little consideration they had for the sun.
sentences.zh: 他们对太阳也毫无考量。

sentences.en: Like it is telling to me that there's this denial of reality that goes along with this denial of human rights.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这种对现实的否认与对人权的否认如出一辙，这很能说明问题。

sentences.en: Like it's not surprising to me that those two things go together.
sentences.zh: 这两者联系在一起，我一点也不感到惊讶。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, it got really intense there at the end.
sentences.zh: 好吧，最后那部分确实很沉重。

sentences.en: I thought we were just going to talk about time zones.
sentences.zh: 我还以为我们只是要讨论时区问题。

sentences.en: Well, that was incredibly fascinating.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那真是太引人入胜了。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: When we come back, Chris Berube on the surprisingly controversial issue of springing forward and falling back after this.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，克里斯·伯鲁比将讨论关于“夏令时”这一令人惊讶的争议话题，广告之后见。

sentences.en: So I'm here with Chris Berube.
sentences.zh: 我现在和克里斯·伯鲁比在一起。

sentences.en: And Chris, you want to talk about one of the great time-related debates.
sentences.zh: 克里斯，你想谈谈关于时间最伟大的辩论之一。

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I want to talk to you today about daylight saving time.
sentences.zh: 今天我想和你谈谈夏令时。

sentences.en: And so I always say daylight savings time.
sentences.zh: 我总是说“Daylight savings time”。

sentences.en: Is it not daylight savings time?
sentences.zh: 难道不是叫“Daylight savings time”吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 绝对不是。

sentences.en: That is not what I'm here to talk about.
sentences.zh: 那不是我要谈的内容。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: In all the legislation that has made DST, daylight saving time, happen, they drop the S.
sentences.zh: 在所有制定夏令时（DST，Daylight Saving Time）的法律中，他们都去掉了那个“S”。

sentences.en: But that's not the controversy around it.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是围绕它的争议所在。

sentences.en: There's other controversies related to daylight saving time.
sentences.zh: 关于夏令时还有其他争议。

sentences.en: It's something that, you know, people around the world kind of take for granted in large parts of North America and Europe and South America.
sentences.zh: 在北美、欧洲和南美的大部分地区，人们对它习以为常。

sentences.en: And you know how daylight saving time works.
sentences.zh: 你知道夏令时是如何运作的。

sentences.en: It's in the summer, we spring forward one hour.
sentences.zh: 在夏天，我们将时钟拨快一小时。

sentences.en: So that's actually the daylight being saved is the extra daylight in the evening when the sun sets later.
sentences.zh: 所以所谓的“节省日光”，其实就是当太阳落山较晚时，傍晚多出的那段日光。

sentences.en: And then around October, it falls back.
sentences.zh: 然后大约在十月，时钟会拨回。

sentences.en: So then you lose an hour and you have an earlier sunset.
sentences.zh: 这样你就失去了一小时，日落时间也提前了。

sentences.en: And it's something that I've been used to because I've had it my whole life.
sentences.zh: 我对此已经习惯了，因为我一生都在经历它。

sentences.en: It's just a thing that happens twice a year.
sentences.zh: 这只是每年发生两次的事情。

sentences.en: But it's actually really controversial.
sentences.zh: 但它实际上非常有争议。

sentences.en: And there are people who are trying to change the future of daylight saving time right now.
sentences.zh: 现在有些人正试图改变夏令时的未来。

sentences.en: And that's what I want to talk about.
sentences.zh: 这就是我想谈的。

sentences.en: But before we get to that, Roman, do you know where daylight saving time comes from?
sentences.zh: 但在那之前，罗曼，你知道夏令时是从哪里来的吗？

sentences.en: I was always told that it was because of farmers, that they needed more daylight to do farming.
sentences.zh: 我一直被告知是因为农民，因为他们需要更多的日光来耕作。

sentences.en: That is not at all the case.
sentences.zh: 事实根本不是这样。

sentences.en: Much like daylight savings time, it is a myth that it's about farmers.
sentences.zh: 就像“Daylight savings time”这个叫法一样，关于农民的说法也是一个神话。

sentences.en: And I know that because I called this guy.
sentences.zh: 我知道这一点是因为我采访了这个人。

sentences.en: This is Dr. David Prerow.
sentences.zh: 这位是大卫·普雷罗博士。

sentences.en: I'm the author of the book Seize the Daylight, the curious and contentious story of daylight saving time.
sentences.zh: 我是《抓住日光：关于夏令时好奇而充满争议的故事》一书的作者。

sentences.en: He actually is the world expert on the subject of DSt.
sentences.zh: 他实际上是夏令时领域的世界级专家。

sentences.en: I don't like to say that, but some people have said that.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢这么说，但确实有人这么评价过。

sentences.en: When people find out that you are a daylight saving expert, do they get mad at you?
sentences.zh: 当人们发现你是夏令时专家时，他们会生你的气吗？

sentences.en: Are they like, because I feel like it is a charged thing.
sentences.zh: 他们会吗？因为我觉得这是一个很敏感的话题。

sentences.en: Like people have strong opinions about it.
sentences.zh: 人们对此有强烈的看法。

sentences.en: Well, what happens is when they lose an hour, the day they lose the hour of sleep, everybody gets mad at me.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当他们失去一小时睡眠的那天，每个人都会生我的气。

sentences.en: The day they sleep an extra hour, nobody comes and thanks me.
sentences.zh: 当他们多睡一小时的那天，却没人来感谢我。

sentences.en: So when I was talking to Dr. Prerow, I brought up the farmer thing that everyone seems to think about daylight saving.
sentences.zh: 所以当我和普雷罗博士交谈时，我提到了每个人似乎都认为的关于夏令时的农民说法。

sentences.en: And what he told me is it's a total myth.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，那完全是个神话。

sentences.en: Farmers, many people think daylight saving time was put in to help the farmers.
sentences.zh: 很多人认为夏令时是为了帮助农民而设立的。

sentences.en: And it's the exact 100 percent opposite.
sentences.zh: 事实恰恰相反，完全相反。

sentences.en: They have to follow the sun independent of what the clock says.
sentences.zh: 无论时钟怎么走，他们都必须遵循太阳的规律。

sentences.en: So you might say, so what?
sentences.zh: 你可能会说，那又怎样？

sentences.en: Let them just do it and, you know, let everybody else change their clock.
sentences.zh: 让他们自己按太阳作息，让其他人去改时钟不就行了。

sentences.en: But the problem is that farmers have to interact with the rest of the world.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，农民必须与世界其他地方进行互动。

sentences.en: They have to bring products to market.
sentences.zh: 他们必须把农产品推向市场。

sentences.en: So farmers have to get up with the sun and the businesses they're working with are using the clock.
sentences.zh: 所以农民必须随太阳起床，而他们合作的企业却在使用时钟。

sentences.en: So it's inconvenient when twice a year the clock based businesses are shifting their time around.
sentences.zh: 因此，当那些以时钟为准的企业每年两次调整时间时，这很不方便。

sentences.en: So the headline here is Farmers Are Not Responsible for Daylight Saving Time.
sentences.zh: 所以结论是：农民并不对夏令时负责。

sentences.en: The credit slash blame belongs to a British house builder named William Willett.
sentences.zh: 这项功劳或罪名属于一位名叫威廉·威利特的英国建筑商。

sentences.en: And each morning he'd wake up at sunrise, go out for a horseback ride around his area.
sentences.zh: 每天早上他都会在日出时醒来，骑马在附近转转。

sentences.en: And while he was on one of these morning horseback rides, he would realize that everybody else is asleep
sentences.zh: 在这些晨间骑行中，他意识到其他人还在睡觉，

sentences.en: and they're not making good use of the beautiful spring and summer mornings.
sentences.zh: 他们没有好好利用美丽的春夏早晨。

sentences.en: So he wrote this pamphlet called A Waste of Daylight.
sentences.zh: 于是他写了一本名为《浪费日光》的小册子。

sentences.en: He wrote this pamphlet promoting the idea of pushing back the clocks one hour in the summer.
sentences.zh: 他在小册子里提倡在夏天将时钟拨快一小时的想法。

sentences.en: And it was really influential.
sentences.zh: 这非常有影响力。

sentences.en: And the British Parliament actually took up his idea.
sentences.zh: 英国议会甚至采纳了他的想法。

sentences.en: That's how influential his pamphlet became.
sentences.zh: 他的小册子影响力就是这么大。

sentences.en: Well, and did they approve it based off his pamphlet?
sentences.zh: 那么，他们是根据他的小册子批准的吗？

sentences.en: They did not.
sentences.zh: 并没有。

sentences.en: So some politicians argued this was a completely pointless thing.
sentences.zh: 一些政客认为这完全是毫无意义的事情。

sentences.en: They were like, hey, if you want more daylight, why don't you just wake up earlier?
sentences.zh: 他们说，嘿，如果你想要更多的日光，为什么不早点起床呢？

sentences.en: Wake up earlier.
sentences.zh: 早点起床。

sentences.en: Yeah, it seemed intuitive to them.
sentences.zh: 是的，这对他们来说似乎很直观。

sentences.en: So they rejected it.
sentences.zh: 所以他们拒绝了。

sentences.en: But Willard was not the type to be dissuaded.
sentences.zh: 但威利特不是那种容易被劝阻的人。

sentences.en: So the next year he came back again with the same proposal and the same proposal the next year
sentences.zh: 所以第二年他又带着同样的提案回来了，接下来的每一年也是如此，

sentences.en: and the next year as it kept being considered but rejected.
sentences.zh: 尽管提案一直被审议但都被拒绝了。

sentences.en: And this became a perennial piece of legislation.
sentences.zh: 这成了每年都会提出的立法议题。

sentences.en: So actually like Winston Churchill became a champion of this.
sentences.zh: 实际上，温斯顿·丘吉尔成了这一主张的支持者。

sentences.en: He was the headline speaker at a big rally for Daylight Saving.
sentences.zh: 他曾是夏令时大型集会上的主讲人。

sentences.en: But it was rejected in 1911.
sentences.zh: 但它在1911年被拒绝了。

sentences.en: It was rejected in 1912.
sentences.zh: 1912年被拒绝了。

sentences.en: It was rejected in 1913.
sentences.zh: 1913年被拒绝了。

sentences.en: It was rejected in 1914.
sentences.zh: 1914年被拒绝了。

sentences.en: And then...
sentences.zh: 然后……

sentences.en: In 1915, unfortunately, Willard passed away.
sentences.zh: 1915年，不幸的是，威利特去世了。

sentences.en: Never to ever see his idea come to fruition.
sentences.zh: 他永远没能看到他的想法实现。

sentences.en: If Willard had lived one more year, he would have seen his idea implemented.
sentences.zh: 如果威利特多活一年，他就能看到他的想法被实施了。

sentences.en: Because in 1916, World War I was in full swing.
sentences.zh: 因为在1916年，第一次世界大战正如火如荼地进行。

sentences.en: And across all of the countries fighting in the war, there was an energy crisis because a lot of coal miners had joined the military.
sentences.zh: 在所有参战国中，都出现了能源危机，因为许多煤矿工人都参军了。

sentences.en: So they wanted to save energy because there wasn't enough coal miners to actually provide the energy that they needed to run the country.
sentences.zh: 所以他们想节省能源，因为没有足够的煤矿工人来提供国家运行所需的能源。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Germany, we're the first country to realize like, hey, one great way to save energy is to do this Daylight Saving thing that Britain has been considering for all these years.
sentences.zh: 德国是第一个意识到“嘿，节省能源的一个好方法就是实施英国考虑了这么多年的夏令时”的国家。

sentences.en: So Germany brings it in and then immediately Britain becomes really jealous.
sentences.zh: 于是德国实施了它，英国立刻变得非常嫉妒。

sentences.en: Within a month, after having rejected it for seven or eight years, within a month of the Germans putting it in, the British put it in.
sentences.zh: 在拒绝了七八年之后，德国人实施后的一个月内，英国人也实施了。

sentences.en: And eventually the countries put it in on both sides of the war.
sentences.zh: 最终，战争双方的国家都实施了它。

sentences.en: And that's how we got Daylight Saving is because of World War I.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们得到夏令时的原因，是因为第一次世界大战。

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: And also keeping up with the Joneses during World War I, which is an amazing part of that story.
sentences.zh: 而且在第一次世界大战期间还要跟风攀比，这是故事中令人惊叹的一部分。

sentences.en: Yeah, it might be more accurate to say we got it because of World War I and jealousy.
sentences.zh: 是的，更准确的说法可能是我们是因为第一次世界大战和嫉妒才有了它。

sentences.en: Those are the causes of it.
sentences.zh: 这些就是原因。

sentences.en: And actually, at first it was really complicated.
sentences.zh: 事实上，起初它非常复杂。

sentences.en: It was a big problem because people kept breaking their clocks because the clocks were not built in a way that you could manually move the hour hands back and forth.
sentences.zh: 这是一个大问题，因为人们不断弄坏他们的时钟，因为当时的钟表设计不支持手动来回拨动时针。

sentences.en: But fast forward a hundred years and throughout the last century, most of Europe adopted Daylight Saving time.
sentences.zh: 但快进一百年，在上个世纪，欧洲大部分地区都采用了夏令时。

sentences.en: It spreads to North America.
sentences.zh: 它传播到了北美。

sentences.en: Countries around the world have tried using it on and off.
sentences.zh: 世界各地的国家都尝试过时断时续地使用它。

sentences.en: And what we see now is about 70 countries worldwide have Daylight Saving time.
sentences.zh: 我们现在看到全球约有70个国家实行夏令时。

sentences.en: And even though it's common, it's still pretty controversial.
sentences.zh: 尽管它很普遍，但仍然相当有争议。

sentences.en: Like, I grew up in Canada.
sentences.zh: 比如，我在加拿大长大。

sentences.en: I really like Daylight Saving time in the summer because you get that extra sunlight in the evening.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢夏天的夏令时，因为傍晚能多出额外的阳光。

sentences.en: But I'll say during Canadian winters when Daylight Saving time goes away and we go back to Standard time, it can be brutal.
sentences.zh: 但我得说，在加拿大漫长的冬天，当夏令时结束，我们回到标准时间时，那简直是残酷的。

sentences.en: Like, there are parts of Canada where you could just get these really early sunsets.
sentences.zh: 加拿大有些地方日落时间会变得非常早。

sentences.en: Well, that part of Daylight Saving, it's not that I have a problem with Daylight Saving in terms of, like, I think it should be there all the time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，关于夏令时的那部分，并不是说我对夏令时本身有意见，比如我觉得它应该一直存在。

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你明白我的意思吗？

sentences.en: Like, I don't understand why it needs to fall back, I think is the thing.
sentences.zh: 我不明白为什么它非得拨回去，我觉得这才是问题所在。

sentences.en: So my sense of the controversy is the period of time that is not Daylight Saving time, not the part that is.
sentences.zh: 所以我对这场争议的理解是，它针对的是非夏令时的时间段，而不是夏令时那部分。

sentences.en: Does that make sense?
sentences.zh: 这说得通吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, and you're not alone in that position at all, because about 10 years ago,
sentences.zh: 没错，而且你完全不是唯一持这种观点的人，因为大约 10 年前，

sentences.en: there was a political movement in the United Kingdom where this whole idea comes from to take Daylight Saving time and push it even further.
sentences.zh: 英国发起了一场政治运动，也就是这个想法的起源，旨在将夏令时进一步推行。

sentences.en: Oh, that's exciting.
sentences.zh: 哦，那太令人兴奋了。

sentences.en: Well, here's a question.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这里有个问题。

sentences.en: Could this weekend be the last time we put the clocks back?
sentences.zh: 这个周末会是我们最后一次拨回时钟吗？

sentences.en: Assuming you remember to, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，前提是你记得要拨的话。

sentences.en: Well, there are growing calls this lunchtime for exactly that, saying the current system is outdated.
sentences.zh: 嗯，今天午间新闻里有越来越多的呼声正是针对这一点，称现行制度已经过时了。

sentences.en: You go to work is dark.
sentences.zh: 你出门上班时天是黑的。

sentences.en: You come home is dark.
sentences.zh: 你下班回家时天也是黑的。

sentences.en: Hate it.
sentences.zh: 讨厌这样。

sentences.en: Perhaps we should do with an extra hour light.
sentences.zh: 也许我们应该多争取一小时的光照。

sentences.en: Get a lot more done when it's light.
sentences.zh: 天亮的时候能多做很多事。

sentences.en: Children can play out longer.
sentences.zh: 孩子们也能在外面多玩一会儿。

sentences.en: And it became this really popular campaign.
sentences.zh: 于是这变成了一场非常受欢迎的运动。

sentences.en: It actually had a catchy name.
sentences.zh: 它甚至有个朗朗上口的名字。

sentences.en: The name of the campaign was Lighter Later.
sentences.zh: 这场运动的名字叫“晚间更亮”（Lighter Later）。

sentences.en: Lighter Later.
sentences.zh: “晚间更亮”。

sentences.en: Joining me now at Lighter...
sentences.zh: 现在加入我的是“晚间更亮”……

sentences.en: Lighter...
sentences.zh: “晚间更亮”……

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: Lighter Later Campaign.
sentences.zh: “晚间更亮”运动。

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: Lighter Later Campaign.
sentences.zh: “晚间更亮”运动。

sentences.en: This is Daniel.
sentences.zh: 这位是丹尼尔。

sentences.en: Yeah, memorable name.
sentences.zh: 没错，名字挺好记的。

sentences.en: Really hard to say.
sentences.zh: 真的很难说出口。

sentences.en: That campaign actually proposed that we double daylight saving time in the summer.
sentences.zh: 那场运动实际上提议在夏季将夏令时翻倍。

sentences.en: You're going to have to explain what that means, because I have a very tenuous grasp on daylight saving, as it is.
sentences.zh: 你得解释一下那是什么意思，因为我对夏令时的理解本来就很模糊。

sentences.en: So, it's complicated, but please bear with me.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这很复杂，但请耐心听我说。

sentences.en: So, under Lighter Later, you'd have an extra hour of daylight in the winter.
sentences.zh: 根据“晚间更亮”计划，你在冬天会多出一小时的日光。

sentences.en: Basically, you wouldn't do the fallback.
sentences.zh: 基本上，你不需要把时钟拨回去。

sentences.en: You wouldn't fallback.
sentences.zh: 你不需要拨回。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then, just for a treat, just for fun, let's actually give ourselves one other hour of daylight in the summer.
sentences.zh: 然后，作为一种福利，纯粹为了好玩，我们再在夏天给自己增加一小时的日光。

sentences.en: So, basically, the clocks will move forward one hour all year round.
sentences.zh: 所以，基本上，时钟全年都会向前拨快一小时。

sentences.en: In the winter in Great Britain, you'd be on summertime, and in the summer, you'd be on something called double summertime.
sentences.zh: 在英国，冬天你会处于夏令时，而夏天你会处于所谓的“双重夏令时”。

sentences.en: So, it just shifts everything.
sentences.zh: 所以，这只是把一切都往后移了。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And when this campaign was rolling out, they were listing all these benefits.
sentences.zh: 当这场运动开展时，他们列举了所有这些好处。

sentences.en: And, like, just listen to the list of benefits of double daylight saving time.
sentences.zh: 而且，你听听这些双重夏令带来的好处清单。

sentences.en: It sounds really good.
sentences.zh: 听起来真的很不错。

sentences.en: It's claimed the overall health of the nation would improve as people could enjoy daylight for longer.
sentences.zh: 据称，由于人们可以享受更长时间的日光，国民的整体健康状况会得到改善。

sentences.en: Children, they'd benefit, as many of them aren't allowed to leave their homes after dark.
sentences.zh: 孩子们也会受益，因为他们中许多人在天黑后是不被允许出门的。

sentences.en: They'd be able to play outside for longer.
sentences.zh: 他们将能在外玩耍更长时间。

sentences.en: It's estimated up to 100 road deaths could be prevented annually across Britain due to better visibility.
sentences.zh: 据估计，由于能见度提高，英国每年可减少多达 100 起道路死亡事故。

sentences.en: And around 450,000 tons of CO2 would be saved by people switching their lights on later.
sentences.zh: 而且由于人们开灯的时间推迟，大约可以节省 45 万吨二氧化碳。

sentences.en: It's great for the environment.
sentences.zh: 这对环境很有利。

sentences.en: It's great for safety.
sentences.zh: 这对安全很有利。

sentences.en: It's great for health.
sentences.zh: 这对健康很有利。

sentences.en: Like, what is not to love about this idea?
sentences.zh: 你说，这个想法有什么不让人喜欢的呢？

sentences.en: I mean, it sounds fantastic.
sentences.zh: 我是说，听起来太棒了。

sentences.en: It does seem like as you begin to creep up even further, it'd be really dark in the morning, right?
sentences.zh: 但似乎当你开始进一步推行时，早晨会变得非常黑，对吧？
哦，百分之百会。

sentences.en: But, I mean, just think about all those benefits, right?
sentences.zh: 但是，我是说，想想所有这些好处，对吧？

sentences.en: The argument they always made was like, look, yes, obviously it would be darker in the morning than we're used to.
sentences.zh: 他们一直以来的论点是，看，是的，显然早晨会比我们习惯的要黑。

sentences.en: But the benefits outweigh that one negative part of this.
sentences.zh: 但好处超过了这唯一负面的一点。

sentences.en: So, in 2012, the UK Parliament actually decided to take up this idea.
sentences.zh: 所以，在 2012 年，英国议会实际上决定采纳这个想法。

sentences.en: And it felt like one of those few things that everybody could agree on.
sentences.zh: 这感觉像是少数大家都能达成共识的事情之一。

sentences.en: So, environmentalists liked it.
sentences.zh: 所以，环保主义者喜欢它。

sentences.en: Business leaders liked it.
sentences.zh: 商界领袖喜欢它。

sentences.en: Also, politically, labor politicians were in favor of it.
sentences.zh: 而且在政治上，工党政客支持它。

sentences.en: And so were the conservatives.
sentences.zh: 保守党也是。

sentences.en: Actually, it was a conservative MP named Rebecca Harris who proposed launching this, like, pilot project for later, later.
sentences.zh: 事实上，是一位名叫丽贝卡·哈里斯的保守党议员提议启动这个“晚间更亮”的试点项目。

sentences.en: She's the one who put forward the legislation.
sentences.zh: 是她提出了这项立法。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: All political persuasions enjoy the sun.
sentences.zh: 所有政治派别都喜欢阳光。

sentences.en: That's the idea.
sentences.zh: 这就是初衷。

sentences.en: So, Rebecca Harris puts it forward.
sentences.zh: 所以，丽贝卡·哈里斯提出了这个方案。

sentences.en: About 120 members of Parliament say they're going to support the bill.
sentences.zh: 大约 120 名议会议员表示他们会支持该法案。

sentences.en: Polls show it's really popular.
sentences.zh: 民调显示它非常受欢迎。

sentences.en: It looks like it's just going to cruise.
sentences.zh: 看起来它会顺利通过。

sentences.en: Like, it's going to be a slam dunk once the legislation reaches the House.
sentences.zh: 一旦立法提交到议会，这简直是板上钉钉的事。

sentences.en: And it comes up for debate in 2012.
sentences.zh: 结果它在 2012 年进入辩论环节。

sentences.en: And?
sentences.zh: 然后呢？

sentences.en: You're setting this up for this not happening.
sentences.zh: 你这么说，看来是没成。

sentences.en: So, what actually ended up happening is that members of Rebecca Harris' own party filibustered the bill.
sentences.zh: 所以，最终发生的情况是，丽贝卡·哈里斯自己党派的成员对该法案进行了阻挠议事。

sentences.en: Oh, why?
sentences.zh: 哦，为什么？

sentences.en: Roman, you may be disappointed to hear this, but it's all because of your friends in Scotland.
sentences.zh: 罗曼，听到这个你可能会失望，但这全是因为你在苏格兰的朋友们。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: Well, I want to hear their take on it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我想听听他们的看法。

sentences.en: Because usually me and the Scots see eye to eye in most things.
sentences.zh: 因为通常我和苏格兰人在大多数事情上意见一致。

sentences.en: You're pretty much on the same page always, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想你们总是意见高度一致。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, Roman, I mean, just think about where, like, Scotland is geographically in the UK.
sentences.zh: 所以，罗曼，我是说，想想苏格兰在英国的地理位置。

sentences.en: So, where is it?
sentences.zh: 那它在哪儿？

sentences.en: Like, if you look at a map of the UK where it's Scotland.
sentences.zh: 如果你看一眼英国地图，苏格兰在哪儿。

sentences.en: It's right about north of England.
sentences.zh: 就在英格兰北边。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, they have a different climate from the legislators down in England who are putting this forward.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们的气候与英格兰那些提出这项法案的立法者们不同。

sentences.en: And for them, the idea of having lighter later mostly means that they're going to have much later sunrises than everybody else.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，“晚间更亮”的想法主要意味着他们的日出时间会比其他任何地方都要晚得多。

sentences.en: So, the whole line was, we're about to have another referendum on Scotland staying in the United Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 所以，当时的口径是，我们即将就苏格兰是否留在英国进行另一次公投。

sentences.en: And this feels like it is those big, bad politicians down in London making Scotland live a certain way.
sentences.zh: 这感觉就像是伦敦那些高高在上的政客强迫苏格兰人过某种生活方式。

sentences.en: And, you know, this is government overreach.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这是政府越权。

sentences.en: And it's like ammunition for these people who are campaigning for Scottish independence.
sentences.zh: 这简直是给那些争取苏格兰独立的人提供了弹药。
