sentences.en: So, all of a sudden, there's a couple of MPs who are like, oh, well, the most important thing is we have to make sure Scotland stays in the UK.
sentences.zh: 所以，突然之间，有几个议员觉得，哦，好吧，最重要的事情是我们必须确保苏格兰留在英国。

sentences.en: So, that's how we end up seeing a couple of rogue MPs turning on this bill.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是为什么我们最终看到几个不听话的议员反对这项法案。

sentences.en: Roman, have you ever heard of a guy named Jacob Rees-Mogg?
sentences.zh: 罗曼，你听说过一个叫雅各布·里斯-莫格的人吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: So, Jacob Rees-Mogg is a politician in the UK who is very pro-Brexit.
sentences.zh: 雅各布·里斯-莫格是英国的一位政客，非常支持脱欧。

sentences.en: He's a very prominent person in Boris Johnson's government.
sentences.zh: 他是鲍里斯·约翰逊政府中非常显眼的人物。

sentences.en: He's the house leader.
sentences.zh: 他是下议院领袖。

sentences.en: But for our purposes, the reason he's important is because he is a gigantic troll.
sentences.zh: 但对我们来说，他之所以重要，是因为他是个彻头彻尾的喷子。

sentences.en: And Jacob Rees-Mogg came out very much against this bill.
sentences.zh: 雅各布·里斯-莫格非常明确地反对这项法案。

sentences.en: The problem with the daylight saving bill, as it's called, is it doesn't save any daylight because there's only a limited amount.
sentences.zh: 所谓的夏令时法案的问题在于，它根本节省不了任何日光，因为日光总量是有限的。

sentences.en: And in the winter, not a lot of it.
sentences.zh: 而且在冬天，日光并不多。

sentences.en: Not a lot.
sentences.zh: 不多。

sentences.en: And I think changing the clocks is a basically fruitless exercise.
sentences.zh: 我认为改变时钟基本上是徒劳的。

sentences.en: So, Jacob Rees-Mogg, being a giant political troll, decides the best thing that he can do is basically put in a poison pill amendment to try and kill this legislation.
sentences.zh: 所以，雅各布·里斯-莫格作为一个政治喷子，决定他能做的最好的事就是加入一个“毒丸”修正案，试图扼杀这项立法。

sentences.en: So, he proposes that Somerset, the area he represents in England, should have its own time zone that is 15 minutes behind the rest of the United Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 于是他提议，他所代表的英格兰萨默塞特郡应该拥有自己的时区，比英国其他地区慢 15 分钟。

sentences.en: Oh, goodness.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: And it was this very attention-grabbing idea.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常吸引眼球的想法。

sentences.en: Suddenly, people weren't talking about daylight saving time anymore.
sentences.zh: 突然间，人们不再谈论夏令时了。

sentences.en: They were talking about this idea of Somerset time.
sentences.zh: 他们都在谈论这个“萨默塞特时间”的想法。

sentences.en: And Jacob Rees-Mogg went on the BBC to explain it and also kind of get like a light ribbing for proposing this idea.
sentences.zh: 雅各布·里斯-莫格上了 BBC 节目来解释这一点，同时也因为提出这个想法而受到了一些轻微的嘲讽。

sentences.en: Correct me if I'm wrong, but hasn't Somerset always been 15 minutes behind the rest of us?
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，萨默塞特郡不是一直比我们其他人慢 15 分钟吗？

sentences.en: In many ways, Somerset is a head of the rest of the country and a leader in all things.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，萨默塞特都领先于全国其他地区，是万事之先驱。

sentences.en: What you're trying to do is sabotage the bill to move the clocks forward, correct?
sentences.zh: 你试图做的是破坏这项拨快时钟的法案，对吧？

sentences.en: Basically, yes.
sentences.zh: 基本上，是的。

sentences.en: The bill comes up for debate and they spend a lot of time talking about Scotland.
sentences.zh: 法案进入辩论阶段，他们花了大量时间讨论苏格兰问题。

sentences.en: A little bit of time talking about the joke idea in Somerset.
sentences.zh: 花了一点时间讨论萨默塞特那个开玩笑的想法。

sentences.en: But in the end, the dissident MPs are able to talk out the bill.
sentences.zh: 但最终，那些持异议的议员成功地通过辩论拖垮了法案。

sentences.en: Basically, they just debate it long enough that the clock runs out and the bill just dies.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们辩论的时间足够长，直到时间耗尽，法案就此夭折。

sentences.en: So, there's really like a classic filibuster.
sentences.zh: 所以，这确实是一场典型的阻挠议事。

sentences.en: They like ran out the clock from talking and then they died.
sentences.zh: 他们通过不停地说话耗尽了时间，然后法案就死了。

sentences.en: So, there is sort of widespread support.
sentences.zh: 所以，虽然有广泛的支持。

sentences.en: There's some, you know, valid reasons to not because I'm always on the side of Scotland, to tell you the truth.
sentences.zh: 也有一些合理的反对理由，因为说实话，我总是站在苏格兰这一边。

sentences.en: And then there's some invalid reasons to not do it, like this trolley guy.
sentences.zh: 然后还有一些不合理的反对理由，比如这个捣乱的家伙。

sentences.en: So, where are we?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们现在处于什么位置？

sentences.en: Like, what are the options now?
sentences.zh: 现在的选择是什么？

sentences.en: Well, the UK isn't getting a second time zone.
sentences.zh: 嗯，英国不会有第二个时区。

sentences.en: Like, they aren't going to give Scotland its own time zone, which could solve some of these probleMs.
sentences.zh: 他们不会给苏格兰自己的时区，尽管那可能会解决其中一些问题。

sentences.en: And the government has said they're not taking up the daylight saving issue anytime soon.
sentences.zh: 政府也表示近期不会处理夏令时问题。

sentences.en: And even if they did implement Lighter Later, there's no guarantee, even with all the support that it has, there's no guarantee that it would be popular.
sentences.zh: 而且即使他们真的实施了“晚间更亮”，也没有保证——即使有这么多支持——它一定会受欢迎。

sentences.en: Because there's something I have been holding back from you, Roman.
sentences.zh: 因为有些事我一直没告诉你，罗曼。

sentences.en: And that is that the UK has actually tried this before.
sentences.zh: 那就是英国其实以前尝试过这个。

sentences.en: So, during World War II, to save energy, they tried switching to double summertime.
sentences.zh: 二战期间，为了节省能源，他们尝试过切换到双重夏令时。

sentences.en: And I talked to our expert, David Praerau, about this.
sentences.zh: 我跟我们的专家大卫·普雷劳谈过这件事。

sentences.en: And he told me people just really hated the dark mornings.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，人们真的非常讨厌黑暗的早晨。

sentences.en: It was considered a wartime measure by a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 很多人认为这是一种战时措施。

sentences.en: A lot of people, especially the rural people, who, again, still had a very large political influence.
sentences.zh: 许多人，尤其是农村地区的人，他们依然拥有很大的政治影响力。

sentences.en: A lot of them felt it was very disruptive to their situation.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人觉得这对他们的生活状况非常具有破坏性。

sentences.en: And were willing to accept it during the war.

sentences.en: And that's not the only experiment that hasn't worked.

sentences.en: So, the UK also tried permanent daylight saving time in the 60s.
sentences.zh: 英国在 60 年代也尝试过永久夏令时。

sentences.en: So, they basically didn't change the clocks.

sentences.en: They just had the later evenings in the winter.

sentences.en: And they switched back.

sentences.en: And here's the wild thing.

sentences.en: The United States tried it during the energy crisis in the 70s.

sentences.en: Oh, I had no idea.
sentences.zh: 噢，我完全不知道。

sentences.en: And people didn't like that either.
sentences.zh: 结果人们还是不喜欢。

sentences.en: And every time this happens, despite all the benefits, despite saving energy and being

sentences.en: better for exercise and saving lives, the dark mornings are the thing that people always

sentences.en: And when they get it, they really hate it.

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.en: we've tried something else, we've tried the later evenings, and then gone back to the

sentences.en: Oh, right.

sentences.en: Oh, my goodness.

sentences.zh: 但归根结底，他只希望人们能审视历史，并对此进行更深入的探讨。

sentences.en: it.
